newsitem.title: CANADA: GOLF-WALKER WINS DU MAURIER CLASSIC WITH RECORD-TYING ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WALKER WINS DU MAURIER CLASSIC WITH RECORD-TYING ROUND.

text.p: Colleen Walker struck a blow for the over-40 crowd Sunday when she claimed her first career major title on the LPGA Tour with an outstanding final round performance in the du Maurier Classic.

Two weeks shy of her 41st birthday, Walker, who gave birth to her first child last October, tied a Glen Abbey course record by firing a bogey-free eight-under-par 65 to claim victory in the year's final major.
"Today was one of the best rounds of my life," said Walker, who began the day four strokes off the lead.
"I never really thought I had a chance, but it was definitely my day. Every time I got close, I holed the putt."

She finished with a 14-under 278, two shots ahead of Sweden's Liselotte Neumann and three better than overnight leader Kelly Robbins, who posted a one-under 72, and Hall of Famer Betsy King, who closed with a 69.
Brandie Burton, who began the day one shot off the pace after vaulting into contention with a third-round 66, struggled to a 75 and finished seven strokes back.
Walker, a 16-year tour veteran, ended a lengthy title-drought with her first victory since 1992.
"After five years, and a baby, I'm finally in the winner's ring," she said after collecting her $108,000 prize.

While the younger generation has dominated the majors on the men's tour this season -- Tiger Woods (the Masters), Ernie Els (U.S. Open) and Justin Leanord (British Open) -- the veterans are showing the youngsters how it's done in the LPGA majors.
Earlier this year, 41-year-old King won the Dinah Shore, 39-year-old Chris Johnson claimed the LPGA Championship and Briton Alison Nicholas, 35, took the U.S. Open title.
For much of Sunday's round it seemed a playoff was beckoning. Entering the final nine holes, no fewer than 10 players were separated by a single shot.
It took something special to take control, and Walker delivered with her flawless round.
She closed by holing a 15-foot birdie putt at the par-five 494-yard 18th, and set off on a jig round the green.
Neumann and Juli Inkster still had a chance to catch Walker with an eagle on 18.

But Neumann, who shot 69, failed even to make birdie, while Inkster, also needing a three to force a playoff, dumped her second shot into the greenside lake. Her bogey six pushed her back into joint fifth with an even-par 73.
